title: Comedian Cody Dahler: We need to take social media seriously
gist: Profile of Cody Dahler, a former DCMS civil servant turned comedian with over two million Instagram followers and nearly a million on TikTok, who explains politics through short-form comedy. He argues political apathy is overstated, that traditional media relies too much on assumed knowledge, and that outlets must adapt delivery, not just distribution, to social media.

insights.claim: Cody Dahler, 30, has more than two million Instagram followers, almost a million on TikTok and over 100,000 subscribers to his podcast The Truth (In My Opinion), built on political comedy for people who might otherwise avoid politics.
insights.speaker: Rohan Banerjee
insights.so_what: Illustrates the scale of audience independent creators can capture for news-adjacent content, competing with legacy media for attention.

insights.claim: Dahler left the Department for Culture, Media and Sport in 2022 to write for BBC Radio 4 shows, but after a viral video chose his own channel over the 'relative stability' of a BBC staff job, finding freelance work brought greater success and career control.

entities: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

insights.claim: Dahler argues political apathy is less common than the 'media class' suggests; people care about policy impacts but journalists' jargon and assumed knowledge shut them out — he heard 'austerity' hundreds of times growing up without understanding it.
insights.speaker: Rohan Banerjee
insights.so_what: Untapped demand exists for accessible political explainers, an opportunity for media formats that simplify.
insights.quote: My experience is that actually people do care, very much, about politics, and the impact of policies on their lives.

insights.claim: Dahler positions his content as built on top of professional journalism rather than replacing it, aiming to make it comprehensible and give viewers peripheral awareness.
insights.speaker: Rohan Banerjee
insights.so_what: Creators act as distribution layer dependent on journalism they don't fund — a value-capture issue for publishers.

insights.claim: Dahler says newspapers and magazines must change how they convey journalism, not just where; simply transferring existing formats to a phone screen doesn't work because delivery, performance and presentation matter.
insights.speaker: Rohan Banerjee
insights.so_what: Publishers' social strategies need format reinvention, implying investment in video/personality-led content.
insights.quote: Simply transferring an existing format to a phone screen doesn’t necessarily make it suited to social media

insights.claim: Dahler concedes social media is a hotbed of misinformation but argues traditional outlets should take it seriously as a tool to inform people in new ways.

insights.so_what: Platforms remain contested ground between misinformation and legitimate news distribution.
